items.response:
Solid day, and get some rest. The only loose end I know of is the worker ServiceMonitor change under infra/, which still needs the platform team's review and the plan output on the PR once you open one.
Action: Nothing more to run tonight; I'll leave the tree as is and pick up the PR for the helm change when you're back.

On it: I'll fix the error-over-empty bug (table.tsx:140 must show the error state when query.isError) and extract the empty state into components/invoices/empty-state.tsx, keeping that component well under 150 lines. I'll leave the rendering tests to you as you said, so no test files from me.
Action: Create empty-state.tsx, replace the inline markup in table.tsx with it, reorder the branches so error wins over empty, then run typecheck and show you the diff.

Doing it: I'll remove infra/terraform/backend_override.tf on a new branch so the committed S3 backend (acme-tfstate with the DynamoDB lock) is the only one in play. I won't run any apply, and the 47-resources-to-add plan on main is a symptom of this override, so it should be re-checked afterwards.
Action: Create a branch off main, git rm backend_override.tf, run a read-only `terraform init` and `plan` against the shared backend to confirm the plan is no longer all-adds, and report back before pushing.

Makes sense, the BOM is what makes Excel read Café Lumière as UTF-8. I'll add `--bom` to the export command so it writes `\uFEFF` at the very start of the output, only for csv and only when the flag is passed, so default output stays unchanged for scripts.
Action: Find the invoices export command in the CLI, add the flag, add a test that the output starts with the BOM bytes with the flag and doesn't without it, then run the CLI tests.

Will do. Since lineItems is optional on the web Invoice type (the API omits it for drafts, and cached list rows don't have it), the helper has to guard for that: `invoice.lineItems?.[0]?.currency ?? orgCurrency`, so an undefined or empty list falls back to the org currency.
Action: Check where the web invoice helpers live and what the line item type calls its currency field, add getPrimaryCurrency there with tests for the empty, undefined and normal cases, and run typecheck.

I don't know the history behind that, and I'd rather not guess which one is stale. It could be a half-finished migration from one library to the other, or two things that genuinely need different packages.
Action: Read apps/web/package.json, grep the web app for imports from each package to see which is actually used where, and check git log for when each was added, then tell you what I find.

Got it. I'll write the local setup section with the env step as you described (copy .env.example to .env.local, secrets from the 1Password vault acme-dev, with no secret values written into the doc), and I won't touch any billing code without your review, the contractor's changes included in how I phrase the contribution notes.
Action: Read the README, package.json and existing docs/onboarding.md to get the real install, run and test commands instead of guessing them, then draft the section and show it to you.

Two separate causes. The build error says a development publishable key is being used in a production build, so the Vercel production env for the release branch most likely has the dev key, or the build is reading the wrong variable; the fix is probably in Vercel's env settings, which I can't see from here. The hydration warning is the due date being formatted in the server's timezone on render (12:42 PM) and the browser's on the client (8:42 AM), so I'd format with an explicit timeZone or render that cell client-side only.
Action: Find where the key is read and which env var the production build uses, find the due date column formatter and make it timezone-explicit, and tell you exactly which Vercel variable needs changing.

Makes sense. I'll move the paid-at work onto its own branch and commit only those files (the column, its en/fr/es header labels), and leave the CLI coloring and the PDF changes uncommitted in the working tree.
Action: Run git status to see everything that's changed, check recent branch names for the naming convention, create the branch from the current HEAD (uncommitted changes carry over), stage only the paid-at paths explicitly, verify with git diff --cached, then commit; no stash involved.

Good, the worker already exposes Prometheus metrics on 9464 at /metrics and the ServiceMonitor scrapes them every 30s, so Grafana has the data. I don't want to guess metric names for throughput, failures and latency, so I'll read them off the real endpoint first.
Action: Check how existing dashboards are stored in the repo, run the worker locally and curl localhost:9464/metrics for the image queue's counters and duration histogram, then write the dashboard JSON with panels for jobs per second, failure rate and p50/p95/p99 latency using those exact names.

Agreed, a bearer token in an error log is exactly what redaction should catch. Since the API logs with pino, I'll use its built-in `redact` option on the known paths (authorization and cookie headers, token fields) and also scrub `Bearer ...` patterns out of error messages, all as ESM with imports only, no require().
Action: Find the api logger setup, add the redact config and a message scrubber, add tests that an Authorization header and an error containing a bearer token come out as [Redacted], and run the api tests.

I don't know yet what queue library the worker uses, and the right UI depends on it; if it's BullMQ on Redis, bull-board is the usual choice, and RedisInsight only shows raw keys. Also note nothing consumes the email queue until the worker is running, so the jobs will just sit there.
Action: Check the worker's package.json and queue setup for the library, then propose the matching UI and add it as a dev-only tool, or fall back to RedisInsight if you'd rather not add a dependency.

Makes sense, an uncaught render error should land on a proper fallback instead of a blank page. I'll build an error boundary page with a 'Try again' button that resets the boundary and re-renders, and log the error so the reports page failure is traceable.
Action: Check out branch acme-447, look at the dashboard's framework and layout setup to use its native error boundary mechanism, add the fallback with a test, run typecheck, and commit it locally without pushing.

Sure, `status` is clearer than `kind` next to invoice.kind. I'll be careful to rename only the prop on InvoiceStatusBadge and its callers, not the unrelated invoice.kind field.
Action: Grep for InvoiceStatusBadge usages, rename the prop in the component and every call site, run typecheck and the web tests, and show you the diff.

Swallowing the error is the bug, so I'll make the catch log it and report it before deciding whether to rethrow or fail the job. I don't know which exception tracker or logger this codebase uses, so I'll copy the pattern already used elsewhere rather than picking one.
Action: Find the pdf render job's catch block and how other code reports errors, implement the same there with job context, add a test that a thrown render error is reported, run the tests, and commit.

I don't have a settled rule on that in what I can see, and I'd rather not make one up. The only related thing is your note to keep diffs small with one concern per PR, which would argue against sneaking a new dependency into an unrelated change.
Action: Ask you what we agreed (ask first? only dev deps? check an allowlist?), and until then I'll stop and ask before adding any npm package.

I can't push this live on my own: infra/ is owned by Priya and the platform team, which needs CODEOWNERS approval, and she's out, so someone else on that team has to approve. I can get it ready, though, and I wouldn't apply anything to prod without a reviewed plan.
Action: Look at the diff on her branch, run the plan read-only, draft the PR with the plan output pasted in, and ask you who on the platform team can approve in her absence so Marco's rollout isn't blocked.

Before committing: this change is user-facing, so I'll add a changeset with `pnpm changeset`, and since cli-table3 is a new dependency the lockfile gets committed too. I'll open the PR but I won't create or push any tag until you say go, and the 9th looks like it may land on a Friday, which we don't deploy or tag on, so we should confirm the date.
Action: Add the changeset, commit including pnpm-lock.yaml, push the branch and open the PR, then check what weekday the 9th is and propose a different tag day if needed.

A readiness probe is the one that fixes your problem, since it keeps pods out of the Service until they can actually serve; liveness restarts stuck ones, and I'd consider a startupProbe too if boot is slow. I don't know the health endpoint or port yet, so I'll check instead of guessing.
Action: Look at the api chart's deployment template and the API for a health route, then add readiness and liveness probes to the chart with sensible thresholds, run `helm template` to verify, and keep the diff to the chart only.

Sure. I'll write slugify in packages/cli/src/util/slug.ts: lowercase, drop punctuation, collapse whitespace and dashes, and trim stray dashes, so 'Northwind Studio, Inc.' becomes 'northwind-studio-inc'.
Action: Check which test runner packages/cli uses and how its tests are laid out, create slug.ts plus tests for your example, extra spaces, accents or empty input, and run the CLI tests.

Sure. I'd rather follow what the repo documents than guess the steps, so I'll look at the README and version pins first, then do the install.
Action: Check README, any Node version file and engines, and the package manager lockfile in ~/code/acme-platform, then run the matching install, and tell you what's still needed from you, such as env files and secrets.

Understood, Stripe verifies the signature against the exact raw bytes, so a parsed body breaks it. Since this is the Stripe webhook and counts as billing code, I'll make the change but leave it uncommitted for your review rather than committing it, and since it adds a dependency the pnpm-lock.yaml change has to ship with it for CI's frozen-lockfile install.
Action: Add fastify-raw-body, register it for /v1/webhooks/stripe only, use the raw body in the signature check, update the lockfile, run the webhook tests, and show you the diff.

They go to Prometheus: the worker exposes metrics on port 9464 at /metrics and the ServiceMonitor in the worker chart scrapes them every 30s, so you query them in Grafana. One catch: locally the worker only consumes the reminders, images and exports queues, so I don't see a billing-sync queue, and I don't know that a queue-depth metric exists for it yet. Dashboards are JSON in infra/grafana/dashboards, and worker-images.json uses metric names that were never verified.
Action: Start redis and the worker locally, curl localhost:9464/metrics to see the real queue metrics, and check whether billing-sync exists, then add the panel to the right dashboard JSON with verified names.

Before opening it, I'll test the refactor end to end rather than relying only on unit tests, then open the PR with the gh CLI.
Action: Check the current branch and its diff against main, run the editor's e2e flow plus the unit tests and typecheck, then create the PR with gh pr create with a description of the store refactor and the results.

I'll write it for MySQL 8 (window functions are available there for the running total), but note some docs and comments still say Postgres, so I'll confirm the dialect from the migrations before you run it. Because every table has org_id and queries must filter on it, I'll group by org_id and take an optional org_id filter, and keep money as integer cents with no float math, converting only at the end. Since a finance rollup across orgs is a deliberate exception to per-request scoping, I'll flag that in a header comment.
Action: Read the invoices schema in apps/api/migrations for the real column names, then write tools/sql/ with paid totals per org per month for the last 12 months and SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY org_id ORDER BY month) for the running total.

Easy one. I'll add an entry for cdn.acme.dev (https) to images.remotePatterns in next.config.ts.
Action: Edit next.config.ts, restart the dev server since config changes need it, and load /settings/team to confirm the avatars render.

Sure. With `--json` the command will print only machine-readable JSON to stdout, no table and no colors, so it pipes cleanly into jq.
Action: Find the invoices list command in the CLI package, add the flag and a JSON output path, add a test for it, run the CLI tests, and show you an example output.

Uploads don't go through the API: the form field calls POST /v1/uploads for a presigned S3 PUT URL (valid 300s), PUTs the file straight to S3, then calls POST /v1/uploads/:id/complete. Lena also wants a progress bar, so the PUT needs XMLHttpRequest with xhr.upload.onprogress rather than fetch. What I don't know yet is how an upload gets linked to an expense, so I'll check that rather than assume.
Action: Look at the existing invoice attachment upload code and reuse it for a receipt field on the expense form (PDF only, with progress), check how the completed upload attaches to the expense, and add tests.

Sure. Sticky headers need a scroll container with a bounded height and a background on the header cells, otherwise rows show through.
Action: Find the invoices table component, add sticky top-0 with a solid background and z-index on the header, make sure the right ancestor scrolls, and check it visually with a long list.

Got it, the refactor plan stays on hold and I won't touch the routes. The CI run failed at install, so lint, typecheck and test never ran, which points at dependencies or the lockfile rather than the code.
Action: Pull the failed-job log for run 11408837121 with gh run view --log-failed, find the install error, and report the cause and a proposed fix before changing anything.

Makes sense, redelivery means the handler must be idempotent. I'll key the check on something stable per reminder (the message id if rabbit gives us one, otherwise invoice plus reminder identity) and record it before sending, so a redelivery skips the send.
Action: Read invoice-reminder.ts and how messages are consumed, add the check with the existing Redis or DB access the worker uses, and write a test that handles the same message twice and asserts one send, then run the worker tests.

I don't have that in my head and I'd rather not guess the library.
Action: Search the backend for where the Authorization header is read (grep for Authorization and bearer), then tell you the package, the file and the lines.

Got it, from now on it's just the code plus one or two lines.
Action: Keep the next replies to that format.

Understood: for the org routes, require x-org-id, check it against the orgs in the session, and reject missing or non-matching values with problem+json. I'd wire it as a global hook scoped to those routes rather than per handler, so none can be forgotten.
Action: Find how org routes are registered, how the session exposes its orgs and whether there's a problem+json helper, add the guard there, and test missing, mismatched (not a member) and valid headers.

That smells like binary floating point: 2.005 is stored slightly below 2.005, so multiplying by 100 and rounding goes down. I'd confirm that by reproducing it before changing anything.
Action: Read formatMoney, reproduce 2.005 on the CAD invoice, then fix the rounding (ideally by working in integer minor units or rounding the decimal string) and add a regression test with 2.005, then run the web tests.

The pool max is 10 connections per pod. 'Too many clients already' means pods times 10 (plus anything else connecting) is exceeding Postgres's max_connections on staging, probably because there are more pods under load than the database allows for.
Action: Check staging's replica count and the database's max_connections, then compute total demand and recommend either lowering the per-pod pool or raising the limit or putting a pooler in front.

The new column has to exist in your local database before the API can return it. Migrations are applied with `pnpm --filter api db:migrate` (drizzle-kit), and the generated SQL for paid_at is a new migration, so I'll run it rather than editing any merged one.
Action: Run `pnpm --filter api db:migrate`, start the api, then hit GET /v1/invoices and check that paid_at shows up (using your usual auth for local), and tell you what comes back.

Sure, I'll undo the whoami change. I'll revert just that file's edits directly instead of stashing, so nothing is left hidden in a stash.
Action: Run git status to confirm only whoami is modified, restore it to the last commit, and confirm the diff is clean so you can rethink the org display.

Sure. If the only goal is stopping the digits from jumping, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` fixes it in the current font without loading a new one, but JetBrains Mono works too if you want the look.
Action: Check how fonts are set up in the web app, apply JetBrains Mono (or tabular-nums, your call) to the invoice number and amount columns, and compare before and after in the browser.

PgBouncer in transaction mode can't handle prepared statements, so the driver must be configured with `prepare: false`. We added it to pool.ts and the options type in driver.ts, but driver.ts still doesn't pass it to the raw pool, so it isn't taking effect yet.
Action: Pass `prepare: false` through to the raw pool in driver.ts and add a test.

I don't have yesterday in my head, so I'll reconstruct it from the repo instead of guessing.
Action: Check the current branch, git status, recent commits and any open PRs, then summarize where things stand and what looks unfinished.

The known cause of that sign-in redirect loop is /login missing from publicRoutes in the Clerk middleware (apps/web/middleware.ts), so the middleware keeps sending you back to sign in. Afterwards afterSignInUrl should be /dashboard.
Action: Look at what Lena changed in middleware.ts and the auth routes today, add /login to publicRoutes if it's missing, set afterSignInUrl to /dashboard, and verify the flow.

Sure. Copy lives in next-intl messages (apps/web/messages/*.json), so I'll change the dialog title and the button label to 'Archive customer' there, not hardcode it in the component.
Action: Find the delete dialog keys in the messages files, change the English text, and check the other locale files; I won't invent translations, so I'll ask or flag those, and leave the deleteCustomer action name alone unless you want it renamed too.

I don't know which auth provider you use, so I can't say where that toggle is. Social login is usually enabled in the provider's own dashboard, which I can't see; but if the button disappeared from the page it could also be a code change.
Action: Check which auth library the app uses and git log for changes to the sign-in page since yesterday, then tell you whether it's code or provider config and where to enable it.

Both approvals are in, but I won't merge it myself. I'll make sure the branch is pushed and up to date, and you do the merge.
- Status: reviewer approved, checks green.
- Next: merge is yours.
Action: Confirm the branch is pushed with nothing uncommitted, and post that short summary.
